findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizing solution in the sanitizing bucket was a mixture of bleach (Chlorine) and detergent. Sanitizing buckets should only have sanitizer and water in them, no additional cleaning chemicals, as the mixture could change the effectiveness of the sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC directed staff to remake all sanitizing buckets with only bleach and water, and from now on have separate buckets for washing with detergent and sanitizing. Inspector recommends marking each bucket to clarify which ones are for sanitizing and which are for washing. Ensure that chemical sanitizers are used per manufacturer’s instructions.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings at the facility. There were a few droppings in the dry storage area, but there was a larger accumulation of droppings to the right of the double door cooler on the cookline. Inspector spoke with the custodian. They are having a small mouse issue throughout the building that started recently. Pest control is performed by AAA Springfield Terminate once a month. They are setting sticky straps throughout the kitchen. The following actions must be taken to eliminate pests at the facility:

- Cleaning must be a priority at the facility, especially deep cleaning under equipment and other hard to reach areas. Remove the current droppings to better monitor the issue moving forward. Communicate where they are seeing droppings appear with the custodian and pest control operator. 
- Seal all possible entry points with steal wool. Inspector observed a hole in the far right corner of the dry storage area with what appeared to be discarded steel wool on the ground. The custodian re-sealed the hole with more steel wool during the inspection. Any other possible entry points into the facility must be sealed. 
- The custodian placed more traps during the inspection in the areas where droppings were observed. Continue to utilize traps to manage pest population. 
- Store boxes at least 6-inches above the ground.
- Remove excess food, cardboard boxes, and other equipment from the facility.
- Food containers must be kept closed to eliminate food sources; especially overnight. 
- Communicate pest sightings and possible entrance points to the custodian and pest control operator. Inspector also suggests increasing the frequency of visits with the pest control company. 

An inspector will return in two weeks (2/4/2026) to check on progress to eliminate pests at the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed the facility could not find the signed employee health reporting forms. The inspector provided the facility with blank copies during the inspection. Ensure that all employees sign the employee health reporting forms. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed numerous cockroaches throughout the facility. All glue traps placed by third party pest control on 12/8/2023 are generally full around the edges with cockroaches. Cockroaches were most prevalent near the dish machine with apparent nests under/within the booster and within the wall of the walk-in cooler. All life stages are observed. Roaches were observed running in and out of the wall of the walk-in cooler. Live roaches were also observed in the walk-in cooler. Food is protected and no pests are observed on food/food-contact surfaces at this time. Person-in-charge reports that the cockroaches have been reported to supervisor and pest-control was at the facility placing glue traps and spraying on 12/8/2023. Ensure that pests are treated before school re-opens on 1/03/2023. Inspector will return on 1/04/2024.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11:  The facility has met with custodial and maintenance and will create a corrective action plan. There are apparent gaps within the walls of the walk-in cooler (exterior seam of walk-in cooler) and around the wall-to-floor areas exterior and interior that should be sealed. Pests seek harborage in areas that are warm and moist. See that any hollow, cracked, damaged surfaces are repaired or sealed. SCDPH met with staff to discuss repair processes. See that you work in a clockwise fashion to look for holes/cracks/crevices in walls and equipment. Seal with caulking. It was noted that the hot water booster to the left of the dish machine likely has hollow legs and holes in the main box. See that this and any other equipment that can be disassembled is opened to allow for pest to bait/treat. Seal after pest has treated. Repair as needed. The facility is also noted to have pests throughout the entirety of the kitchen. Look for gaps and holes in dry storage - seal hollow and opened equipment. 


PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a can of Mother's Maid Vegetarian Beans with a significant dent along the top seam of the can with sharp rough edges. The can was date marked and stocked on the shelf with cans which are in service. Inspector also observed a can of jalepeno peppers also date marked and stocked with in service foods. The cans were immediately removed and separated to be discarded. Corrected on site. Ensure that cans being received from suppliers and being stocked onto shelves are checked for dents along seems which are significant enough to question the integrity of the seal. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Observed a bag of unlabeled white powder dated 8/22 on the back shelf with no labeling. Operator confirmed the food is powdered sugar. A label was placed on the bag during inspection. Ensure that foods are labeled when stored in containers other than the one they came in. Powders can be mistaken for other substances, ensure they are labeled if in working containers. Corrected on site. 

3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.
